$comment: Object types the native Program renderer prepares. One machine-readable claim, read by both
languages, so the Editor cannot promise on-air support the renderer does not provide.
Rust side: services/render-daemon/tests/program_object_types.rs feeds one object of every declared
SceneObjectType through prepare_scene and asserts that exactly these types avoid the
'are NOT rendered' warning. That test asserts behaviour rather than a mirrored list, so the two
sides cannot drift without one of them failing.
Adding a type here without teaching the renderer to prepare it breaks the Rust test, which is the
point: this file records what is, not what is planned.
$note: layer and group are containers: they are never drawn themselves, and resolveSceneObjectHierarchy
folds their transform into their descendants before publication, so their placement does reach a
published frame indirectly. They are listed as not-rendered because prepare_scene skips them, and
the property contract exempts them from the type-level Preview-only downgrade for that reason.
